findings.finding: The parent's coverage AC names a specific verifier — a script that reconciles the routing key set against `ls .rebar/evals/ src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/` and the open `unreliable-criterion:` ticket titles and exits non-zero if any criterion is in neither set — but no sibling's acceptance criteria deliver that union-reconciliation-with-nonzero-exit check. The selector, emitter, admission runner, and self-healing loop each produce pieces (candidates, specs, admitted files, tickets) but none asserts the completion invariant that every routed criterion is in the specs set OR the ticket set.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC to 1cef (which already knows both the routing set and the ticket set) that runs the reconciliation script and asserts a non-zero exit when any routed criterion is uncovered and unticketed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `unreliable-criterion:` ticket reason vocabulary for a residual inline-runnable criterion that yields no admissible fixture (distinct from 'finder not inline-runnable'), so every ticket the Coverage AC requires records an unambiguous, enumerated reason.
evidence: Plan: self-healing loop files 'an unreliable-criterion: ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each' non-inline class.
Plan child decomposition: 'residual gaps + container/ISF criteria -> the self-healing loop, which files the unreliable-criterion: tickets' -- two distinct populations, only one reason token defined.
Coverage AC: the open ticket must record 'why it has none', but a residual inline-runnable criterion with zero admissible fixtures has no reason token defined (distinct from 'not inline-runnable').

The verified DriftEntry.reason enum already distinguishes 'not-inline-admissible' vs 'container-material-unrecoverable' (fixture_admission.py:126,152), showing reason tokens are load-bearing, yet the residual-gap ticket reason is absent from the plan.
findings.finding: The `unreliable-criterion:` ticket reason vocabulary is defined only for the non-inline (container/ISF) class ('finder not inline-runnable'); the reason recorded for a residual criterion that IS inline-runnable but produced no admissible fixture is never specified, though the Coverage AC requires the ticket to record 'why it has none'.
findings.location: Approach ('Only inline-runnable criteria are mined'), Child decomposition (Coverage AC row), Acceptance Criteria (second bullet)
scenarios: An inline-runnable criterion whose every candidate fails to reproduce gets an unreliable-criterion: ticket, but the executor has no specified reason string to record, so the ticket cannot distinguish 'no candidate mined' from 'candidates failed reproduction' from 'not inline-runnable'.
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the ticket reason tokens the self-healing loop may emit, mirroring the DriftEntry.reason enum: e.g. `not-inline-admissible` (container/ISF), `no-candidate-mined`, and `candidates-failed-reproduction` for the residual inline-runnable case, and state which the Coverage-AC verifier accepts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the no-fire predicate (and the corresponding AC) that a candidate is admitted only when its at-review plan text reconstructs with a VERIFIED material_fingerprint, excluding the ~4.3% unverified rows from no-fire evidence.
evidence: Context: 'the committed manifest ... records 6,482 sidecar rows (verified_ratio 0.9568)'
corpus.py:232 gates on `material_fingerprint(ctx, **kwargs) == signed_fingerprint`, so ~4.3% of rows do not verify

The reproduction gate re-runs the Pass-1 finder against current code — it detects a divergent FIRE but a no-fire built on wrong plan text still yields empty findings, i.e. reproduces as no-fire regardless of reconstruction fidelity
Acceptance Criteria only guards missing-cohort rows and reproduction of fire behavior, not reconstruction-verification of no-fire source plans
findings.finding: The no-fire evidence predicate does not state whether reconstructions that failed the corpus verified_fingerprint check are excluded; a no-fire (expect: pass) fixture mined from an unverified (mis-reconstructed) plan would reproduce trivially as no-fire against the wrong text, so the reproduction gate does not catch it (unlike a fire-fixture, whose finder rerun would diverge).
findings.location: Approach -> 'No-fire evidence predicate'; Context cites verified_ratio 0.9568
scenarios: A sidecar row whose at-review plan cannot be re-derived from git (verification miss) is nonetheless emitted as an expect: pass case, encoding a criterion's silence on plan text that was never actually reviewed
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the no-fire predicate: 'and the row's reconstructed plan passes corpus verified_fingerprint (corpus.py:232); unverified reconstructions are skipped, never emitted as expect: pass.' Extend the synthetic-corpus pytest AC to include an unverified-fingerprint row that is skipped.

evidence: Parent AC1: 'A no-fire (expect: pass) case for criterion C is emitted only when C is in the cohort set of some finding on that plan AND no finding on that plan cites C; a row with a missing cohort key is skipped ... verified by pytest over a synthetic corpus with an in-cohort silent plan (emitted), a never-in-cohort plan (skipped), a missing-cohort row (skipped), and a container/ISF-class criterion (excluded from inline mining).'

549b Approach: 'Reproduction consensus — the key fired, or stayed absent, consistently across two or more reviews with equal material_fingerprint. The only signal valid in the no-fire direction.' — no mention of cohort membership as an admission precondition.
549b ACs: none reference `cohort`, in-cohort/never-in-cohort/missing-cohort, or container/ISF exclusion; its no-fire AC only asserts 'advisory for one holding reproduction consensus'.
092c non-goal: 'Deciding which candidates qualify ... the selector owns all of that and this child transcribes'.
findings.finding: The parent's no-fire predicate AC is only partially covered: its cohort-based admission rule and its four required sub-cases (in-cohort silent plan emitted, never-in-cohort plan skipped, missing-cohort row skipped, container/ISF-class criterion excluded from inline mining) are not delivered by any sibling's acceptance criteria. The selector (549b) defines the no-fire direction solely via 'reproduction consensus' (a key that stayed absent across equal-fingerprint reviews) and never references the `cohort` routing-proof precondition, the missing-cohort skip, or the container/ISF exclusion in any of its ACs; the emitter (092c) only transcribes.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 549b's ACs (or split the cohort predicate across 549b for admission and 1cef for container/ISF ticketing) so the four-case synthetic-corpus test the parent AC names is owned and measurable.

evidence: Parent Approach: 'Both non-inline classes still carry a cohort tag, so the selector EXCLUDES them from inline mining and the self-healing loop files an unreliable-criterion: ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each'.
Parent decomposition: 'container/ISF criteria -> the self-healing loop, which files the unreliable-criterion: tickets'.
1cef breaker AC: ticket created only after 'the third consecutive failed run' for reproduction/skipped-unbalanced failures — no path for an immediate not-inline-runnable ticket.
549b ACs: no AC excludes container (G3/G4/decomp-shape) or ISF criteria from the candidate list.
findings.finding: Owned-by-none scope gap: the parent routes container/ISF-class criteria (excluded from inline mining) to the self-healing loop 'which files the unreliable-criterion: ticket (reason: finder not inline-runnable) for each', but no child's acceptance criteria cover this path. The self-healing loop (1cef) creates `unreliable-criterion:` tickets only on the third consecutive failed run (reproduction failure or skipped-unbalanced); it has no AC for a container/ISF criterion whose finder is not inline-runnable, and the selector (549b) has no AC excluding container/ISF criteria from mining.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 549b AC that a container/ISF-class criterion produces a zero-candidate row with reason 'finder not inline-runnable', and a 1cef AC that such a reason files the `unreliable-criterion:` ticket directly rather than waiting for three failed inline runs.

findings.finding: AC #1's verification enumerates 'a container/ISF-class criterion (excluded from inline mining)' as a required case, but no selector-side AC asserts that container/ISF criteria are excluded from inline mining. The decomposition assigns AC #1 to selector+emitter, yet 549b's no-fire AC tests only routed-and-silent / missing-cohort / cited cases, not container/ISF exclusion.
scenarios: The selector emits a container (G3/G4/decomp-shape) or ISF fixture into the manifest; downstream the admission runner scopes it out to drift, but AC #1's promised selector-level exclusion was never asserted, so a regression re-admitting them to inline mining goes uncaught by the AC #1 verification.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 549b with a parameterized test that a seeded container (G3/G4/decomp-shape) or ISF criterion yields no inline candidate row (or an explicit exclusion marker), so AC #1's container/ISF clause is verified where the parent Approach places the behavior.
